node.title: Human Reproduction: Male and female reproductive system; Microscopic anatomy of

questions.stem: Which cells of the seminiferous tubules provide nutrition to the developing male germ cells?
questions.explanation: The seminiferous tubules contain male germ cells (spermatogonia) and the supporting Sertoli cells. The Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells as they develop into sperm. The Leydig or interstitial cells lie outside the tubules and secrete androgens.

optionRationale.2: Leydig cells lie between the tubules and secrete androgens; they do not nourish germ cells.
optionRationale.3: Spermatogonia are the germ cells themselves and are the cells being nourished.
optionRationale.4: Interstitial cells is another name for the Leydig cells, which secrete androgens.

questions.objective: Identify the nutritive cells of the seminiferous tubule

questions.stem: The secretion of the seminal vesicles, which forms a large part of the seminal plasma, is rich in
questions.explanation: The seminal plasma is secreted by the seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands. The secretion of the seminal vesicles is rich in fructose, calcium and some enzymes, and the fructose is a source of energy for the motile sperm.

optionRationale.1: Lactose is the sugar of milk and is not a major component of semen.
optionRationale.3: Glycogen is a storage polysaccharide and is not the main sugar of seminal fluid.
optionRationale.4: Maltose is not the sugar of seminal plasma.

questions.objective: Recall a component of seminal plasma

questions.stem: After the release of the ovum, the remaining part of the Graafian follicle changes into a temporary endocrine structure called the
questions.explanation: After ovulation the remaining follicular cells transform into the corpus luteum under the influence of LH. The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which maintains the endometrium needed for implantation and pregnancy, and if no fertilisation occurs it degenerates.

optionRationale.1: The zona pellucida is the glycoprotein layer around the ovum.
optionRationale.2: The corpus albicans is the scar that remains after the corpus luteum has degenerated.
optionRationale.4: The theca externa is an outer layer of the follicle and is not an endocrine structure formed after ovulation.

questions.stem: The acrosome at the tip of the head of a sperm contains
options: mitochondria that provide energy for swimming
the centrioles that form the tail
the haploid set of ova chromosomes
enzymes that help the sperm to penetrate the ovum
questions.explanation: The acrosome is a cap-like structure on the sperm head filled with hydrolytic enzymes. These enzymes help the sperm to penetrate the layers surrounding the ovum during fertilisation. The mitochondria are in the middle piece, where they supply energy for the movement of the tail.

optionRationale.1: The mitochondria are packed in the middle piece, not in the acrosome.
optionRationale.2: The acrosome is not the site of the centrioles that organise the tail.
optionRationale.3: The sperm nucleus carries the haploid chromosomes of the sperm, not of the ovum, and it lies behind the acrosome.

questions.objective: State the function of the acrosome

questions.stem: The milk-secreting cells of the mammary gland are present in the
questions.explanation: Each lobe of the mammary gland contains clusters of cells called alveoli. The cells of the alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of the alveoli. The alveoli open into mammary tubules, which join to form the mammary duct, the ampulla and finally the lactiferous duct.

optionRationale.1: The mammary ducts carry the milk but do not secrete it.
optionRationale.3: The lactiferous duct is the final duct through which the milk is sucked out.
optionRationale.4: The ampulla is a storage and conducting region connected to the lactiferous duct.

questions.objective: Locate milk secretion in the mammary gland

questions.stem: Entry of additional sperms into the ovum after the first sperm has made contact is prevented by changes in the
questions.explanation: When a sperm contacts the zona pellucida, it induces changes in the membrane of the ovum that block the entry of additional sperms. This ensures that only one sperm fertilises the egg. The sperm then enters the cytoplasm and induces the completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte.

optionRationale.1: The corona radiata is a layer of follicle cells around the zona pellucida and does not block extra sperm.
optionRationale.2: Cervical mucus is outside the fertilisation site and does not act at the ovum.
optionRationale.3: The endometrium is the lining of the uterus and is not involved in blocking sperm entry.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about early embryonic development.
A. Cleavage is a series of mitotic divisions of the zygote.
B. An embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a morula.
C. The inner cell mass of the blastocyst gives rise to the embryo proper.
D. The trophoblast gives rise to the embryo proper.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Mitotic divisions of the zygote are called cleavage, and the embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is the morula, so A and B are correct. In the blastocyst the inner cell mass gives rise to the embryo (C), while the trophoblast forms the outer layer that attaches to the uterus, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Statement C is also correct, so this is incomplete.
optionRationale.2: Statement A is also correct, so this is incomplete.
optionRationale.4: Statement D is false; the trophoblast forms the outer layer that helps in implantation, not the embryo proper.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on cleavage, morula and blastocyst

questions.stem: Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (source) and choose the correct code.

left: D. Progesterone in the luteal phase
right: I. Trophoblast of the embryo and placenta
III. Released from the posterior pituitary

questions.explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin is secreted by the trophoblast and placenta (A-I). Prolactin is made by the anterior pituitary (B-II) and oxytocin is released from the posterior pituitary (C-III). In the luteal phase of the cycle the corpus luteum secretes progesterone (D-IV).

optionRationale.2: A and B are interchanged; prolactin comes from the pituitary, not the trophoblast.
optionRationale.3: C and D are interchanged; oxytocin is not made by the corpus luteum.
optionRationale.4: A and D are interchanged; hCG is not secreted by the corpus luteum.

questions.objective: Match reproductive hormones with their sources

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Fertilisation in humans takes place at the ampullary-isthmic junction of the fallopian tube.
Reason (R): The zygote begins mitotic cleavage as it moves through the isthmus towards the uterus.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The sperm and ovum meet at the ampullary-isthmic junction, so A is true. The zygote does start cleaving while it travels through the isthmus towards the uterus, so R is true as well. But cleavage happens after fertilisation, so it cannot explain the site where fertilisation occurs.

optionRationale.1: Cleavage follows fertilisation and so cannot be the reason for the site of fertilisation.
optionRationale.3: R is true; cleavage starts in the isthmus on the way to the uterus.
optionRationale.4: A is true; the ampullary-isthmic junction is the site of fertilisation.

questions.objective: Place fertilisation and cleavage in the fallopian tube

questions.stem: In a typical human menstrual cycle, the menstrual flow lasts for about
questions.explanation: In a typical 28-day cycle the menstrual phase lasts for about 3 to 5 days, during which the endometrium and blood vessels break down and are shed as the menstrual flow. The proliferative phase then follows, which ends with ovulation at about the 14th day.

optionRationale.1: One to two days is shorter than the usual duration of the flow.
optionRationale.2: Seven to nine days is longer than the usual flow of a normal cycle.
optionRationale.4: Ten to twelve days would overlap the proliferative phase and is not normal.

questions.stem: A human primary spermatocyte at metaphase I contains how many chromosomes and how many chromatids?
questions.explanation: A primary spermatocyte is diploid, so it has 46 chromosomes. DNA replicated before meiosis I, so each chromosome has two sister chromatids, and the cell therefore has 46 x 2 = 92 chromatids. Pairing into 23 bivalents does not change the number of chromosomes.

optionRationale.1: 23 is the haploid number and the cell is still diploid at this stage.
optionRationale.2: 23 chromosomes would be correct for a secondary spermatocyte, but this cell has 46.
optionRationale.3: 46 chromatids would be the number if the chromosomes were not replicated, which is not the case in meiosis I.

questions.objective: Count chromosomes and chromatids in meiosis I

questions.stem: In a woman who does not become pregnant, menstruation begins because
options: progesterone falls as the corpus luteum degenerates
a sharp rise of LH occurs
hCG secretion begins from the placenta
questions.explanation: If the ovum is not fertilised the corpus luteum degenerates. The level of progesterone, which maintained the thick secretory endometrium, then falls, and the endometrium and its blood vessels break down and are shed as menstrual flow. A rise in progesterone would maintain the lining instead.

optionRationale.2: The LH surge triggers ovulation at mid-cycle and is not the cause of menstruation.
optionRationale.3: High oestrogen at mid-cycle causes the LH surge, not menstruation.
optionRationale.4: hCG appears only in pregnancy and helps to maintain the corpus luteum.

questions.objective: Explain the hormonal trigger of menstruation

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about pregnancy.
A. The heart of the embryo is formed after about one month of pregnancy.
B. The first movements of the foetus and the appearance of hair on the head are usually seen in the fifth month.
C. By the end of 12 weeks most of the major organ systems are formed.
D. The foetal ejection reflex triggers the release of prolactin from the mother's pituitary.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The heart forms after about one month, the first foetal movements and head hair appear in the fifth month, and most major organ systems are formed by the end of the first trimester of 12 weeks, so A, B and C are correct. The foetal ejection reflex triggers the release of oxytocin, not prolactin, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Statement C is also correct, so this misses it.
optionRationale.3: Statement D is false, and statement A is left out.
optionRationale.4: Statement D is false, and statement B is left out.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on foetal development and parturition

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones is NOT produced by the placenta?
questions.explanation: The placenta acts as a temporary endocrine tissue and produces human chorionic gonadotropin, human placental lactogen, oestrogens and progesterone, and at a later stage of pregnancy relaxin. FSH is a pituitary hormone, and in pregnancy its level falls as progesterone and oestrogen rise.

optionRationale.1: hCG is produced by the trophoblast and placenta.
optionRationale.2: hPL is produced by the placenta.
optionRationale.4: Progesterone is produced by the placenta, as well as by the corpus luteum.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Spermatogenesis in a boy starts at puberty.
Reason (R): At puberty a marked rise in GnRH acts on the anterior pituitary to release LH and FSH, which act on the Leydig cells and Sertoli cells of the testis.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis begins at puberty because secretion of GnRH rises. GnRH stimulates the anterior pituitary to secrete LH and FSH. LH acts on the Leydig cells to produce androgens, and FSH acts on the Sertoli cells, so both together start the process of sperm formation.

optionRationale.2: R is the hormonal mechanism that actually starts spermatogenesis, so it is the explanation.
optionRationale.3: R is true; LH acts on Leydig cells and FSH on Sertoli cells.
optionRationale.4: A is true; sperm production starts at puberty.

questions.objective: Explain the hormonal start of spermatogenesis
